transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?
I’ve barely been sleeping since the warehouse inspection. I lie there replaying parts of it, and if I do fall asleep, I wake up sweaty and completely alert, like I’m back near the blast.
How long ago did the warehouse blast occur?
About a week ago. It’s been going on since the inspection, when the explosion happened.
Over the past few days, have your symptoms started to ease up at all?
No, not really. It’s been about a week since the warehouse inspection and the explosion, and it hasn’t started easing up.
Have you found yourself trying to avoid thoughts, places, or reminders of the blast?
Yes. I’ve been avoiding the warehouse file, and I let calls about industrial accounts go to voicemail. Even opening those emails makes my stomach drop.
Since the explosion, have you felt emotionally numb or detached from yourself or your surroundings?
I’m not sure what you mean by detached. I haven’t really noticed feeling numb, exactly.
Have you had moments during the day where you felt like the explosion was happening all over again?

Yes. I’ll be reviewing a policy or looking at a loss report, and all of a sudden I see the worker on the floor and the soot in the air. It hits really sharply, and my body reacts before I can stop it.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F43.1 because the symptoms have been present for only about one week, which does not meet the minimum one-month duration criterion required for PTSD, confirming Acute Stress Disorder (F43.0).

inference_history.note: Patient reports intrusive memories, physiological reactivity, and sleep disturbances following a traumatic event (a blast). Initial differential focuses on trauma- and stressor-related disorders.
